title: Historical Background
desc: British constitutional developments in India before 1950 — Company Rule (1773-1858) and Crown Rule (1858-1947)

basic.q: Under the Regulating Act of 1773, the Governor of Bengal was redesignated as the:
basic.e: The Regulating Act of 1773 designated the Governor of Bengal as the 'Governor-General of Bengal' and created a four-member Executive Council; Warren Hastings was the first such Governor-General.

basic.q: The Amending Act of 1781, which rectified defects in the Regulating Act of 1773, is also known as the:
basic.e: The Amending Act of 1781 is also known as the Act of Settlement. It exempted the Governor-General-in-Council from Supreme Court jurisdiction for official acts.

basic.q: Pitt's India Act of 1784 created a new body called the Board of Control to manage the Company's:
basic.e: Pitt's India Act, 1784 let the Court of Directors manage commercial affairs while a new Board of Control managed political affairs, establishing a 'system of double government'.

basic.q: Besides the power to override his council's decisions in special cases, what other position did Lord Cornwallis demand and receive under the Act of 1786?
o: Chief Justice of the Supreme Court
President of the Board of Control
basic.e: Lord Cornwallis, appointed Governor-General of Bengal in 1786, was additionally made Commander-in-Chief, and the Act of 1786 was passed to enable both his demands.

basic.q: The Charter Act of 1793 extended the East India Company's trade monopoly in India for a further period of:
basic.e: The Charter Act of 1793 extended the Company's trade monopoly in India for another 20 years and extended Lord Cornwallis's overriding power to all future Governor-Generals and Governors.

basic.q: The Charter Act of 1813 ended the East India Company's trade monopoly in India, but continued the Company's monopoly over trade in:
basic.e: The Charter Act of 1813 threw open Indian trade to all British merchants but continued the Company's monopoly over tea trade and trade with China.

basic.q: Who became the first Governor-General of India under the Charter Act of 1833?
basic.e: The Charter Act of 1833 made the Governor-General of Bengal the Governor-General of India, vesting him with all civil and military powers; Lord William Bentinck was the first to hold this office.

basic.q: The Charter Act of 1853 established a separate legislative wing of the Governor-General's council, which came to be known as the:
basic.e: The Charter Act of 1853 added six new legislative councillors and established a separate Indian (Central) Legislative Council, which functioned like a mini-Parliament.

basic.q: The Government of India Act of 1858 changed the designation of the Governor-General of India to:
basic.e: The Government of India Act, 1858 made the Governor-General also the Viceroy of India, the direct representative of the Crown; Lord Canning became the first Viceroy.

basic.q: The 'portfolio system', given legal recognition by the Indian Councils Act of 1861, had actually been introduced in 1859 by which Viceroy?
basic.e: Lord Canning introduced the portfolio system in 1859, under which a council member was placed in charge of specific departments; the Indian Councils Act of 1861 formally recognised it.

basic.q: Besides increasing non-official members in the legislative councils, the Indian Councils Act of 1892 gave these councils the power to discuss the budget and:
basic.e: The Indian Councils Act of 1892 enlarged the councils' functions to include discussing the budget and addressing questions to the executive, while keeping an official majority.

basic.q: The Indian Councils Act of 1909, which introduced separate electorates for Muslims, is also known as the:
basic.e: The Indian Councils Act of 1909 is known as the Morley-Minto Reforms (Lord Morley, Secretary of State; Lord Minto, Viceroy), and it 'legalised communalism' via separate Muslim electorates.

basic.q: The Government of India Act of 1919, which introduced dyarchy in the provinces, is also known as the:
basic.e: The Government of India Act, 1919 is known as the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms and introduced 'dyarchy' — a dual scheme of governance — in the provinces.

basic.q: The Simon Commission, appointed in November 1927 to review India's constitutional working, was boycotted by Indian parties chiefly because:
o: It was appointed two years ahead of schedule
It was headed by a former Viceroy
basic.e: The seven-member Simon Commission, headed by Sir John Simon, had no Indian members, leading all Indian parties to boycott it.

basic.q: Mahatma Gandhi undertook a fast unto death in Yerawada Jail to protest the Communal Award's extension of separate electorates to:
basic.e: The 1932 Communal Award extended separate electorates to the depressed classes; Gandhi's protest fast led to the Poona Pact between the Congress and Dr. B.R. Ambedkar.

basic.q: The All-India Federation proposed by the Government of India Act of 1935, comprising provinces and princely states, ultimately:
o: Never came into being, as princely states did not join
Was replaced by two separate federations
basic.e: Though the Government of India Act, 1935 provided for an All-India Federation, it never came into being because the required number of princely states did not join it.

basic.q: The Indian Independence Act of 1947, which ended British rule in India, was based on which plan put forward by Lord Mountbatten on 3 June 1947?
basic.e: Lord Mountbatten's Mountbatten Plan (3 June 1947) for partition was accepted by the Congress and Muslim League and given legal effect through the Indian Independence Act, 1947.

basic.q: In the Interim Government of 1946, who was designated as the Vice-President of the Council (effectively its head under the Viceroy)?
basic.e: In the Interim Government (1946), Jawaharlal Nehru held External Affairs and Commonwealth Relations and was designated Vice-President of the Council, though the Viceroy remained its head.

intermediate.q:
Consider the following statements about the Regulating Act of 1773:
1. It provided for the establishment of a Supreme Court at Calcutta comprising one chief justice and three other judges.
2. It permitted the servants of the Company to engage in private trade after paying a licence fee.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect — the Act actually prohibited Company servants from engaging in private trade or accepting bribes from 'natives'.

intermediate.q:
Consider the following statements about the Amending Act of 1781:
1. It exempted the Governor-General-in-Council from Supreme Court jurisdiction for their official acts.
2. It brought revenue matters within the jurisdiction of the Supreme Court.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect — the Act excluded revenue matters and matters arising from revenue collection from the Supreme Court's jurisdiction.

intermediate.q:
Consider the following statements about Pitt's India Act of 1784:
1. It distinguished between the commercial and political functions of the East India Company.
2. It ended the system of double government that had existed since the Regulating Act of 1773.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect — Pitt's India Act established the system of double government (Court of Directors + Board of Control); it was the Government of India Act, 1858 that later ended it.

intermediate.q:
Consider the following statements about the Charter Act of 1793:
1. It made the Commander-in-Chief a compulsory member of the Governor-General's council.
2. It laid down that Board of Control members and their staff were to be paid out of Indian revenues.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect — the Act provided that the Commander-in-Chief was NOT to be a member of the council unless specifically so appointed.

intermediate.q:
Consider the following statements about the Charter Act of 1813:
1. It asserted the sovereignty of the British Crown over the Company's territories in India.
2. It barred Christian missionaries from entering India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect — the Act actually allowed Christian missionaries to come to India for the purpose of 'enlightening the people'.

intermediate.q:
Consider the following statements about the Charter Act of 1833:
1. It ended the East India Company's activities as a commercial body, making it purely administrative.
2. Its attempt to introduce open competition for civil service selection was implemented without opposition.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect — the open-competition provision was negated after opposition from the Court of Directors and only actually implemented later.

intermediate.q:
Consider the following statements about the Charter Act of 1853:
1. It introduced open competition for recruitment to the covenanted civil service.
2. Like earlier Charter Acts, it fixed a definite term for renewal of the Company's rule.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect — unlike previous Charters, the 1853 Act did not specify a fixed period, signalling that Company rule could be ended at Parliament's will at any time.

intermediate.q:
Consider the following statements about the Government of India Act of 1858:
1. It created the new office of Secretary of State for India.
2. It expanded the Central Legislative Council by adding new legislative councillors.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect — the 1858 Act mainly transferred power from the Company to the Crown and created a 15-member advisory Council of India; it did not alter legislative council composition.

intermediate.q:
Consider the following statements about the Indian Councils Act of 1861:
1. It began the association of Indians with law-making by allowing nomination of non-official Indian members.
2. It further centralised legislative power by removing powers from the Bombay and Madras Presidencies.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect — the Act decentralised by restoring legislative powers to Bombay and Madras, reversing the centralising trend begun by the Regulating Act of 1773.

intermediate.q:
Consider the following statements about the Indian Councils Act of 1892:
1. It maintained an official majority in the Central and provincial legislative councils.
2. It explicitly used the word 'election' for filling non-official seats.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect — the word 'election' was deliberately not used; the process was described as nomination on the recommendation of certain bodies.

intermediate.q:
Consider the following statements about the Indian Councils Act of 1909 (Morley-Minto Reforms):
1. It introduced separate electorates for Muslims for the first time.
2. It gave the provincial legislative councils a non-official majority while retaining an official majority at the Centre.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Both statements are correct. The Act introduced separate Muslim electorates and, while retaining official majority centrally, allowed provincial councils to have a non-official majority.

intermediate.q:
Consider the following statements about the Government of India Act of 1919:
1. It introduced dyarchy at the provincial level by dividing subjects into transferred and reserved categories.
2. It introduced bicameralism and direct elections at the Centre for the first time.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Both statements are correct. The Act introduced provincial dyarchy and, at the Centre, replaced the Indian legislative council with a bicameral legislature chosen largely by direct election.

intermediate.q:
Consider the following statements about the Simon Commission and the Poona Pact:
1. The Simon Commission's 1930 report recommended continuation of the communal electorate.
2. The Poona Pact abolished separate electorates altogether for every community in India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect — the Poona Pact only dropped separate electorates for the depressed classes, retaining joint Hindu electorates with reserved seats; other communities' separate electorates under the Communal Award were unaffected.

intermediate.q:
Consider the following statements about the Government of India Act of 1935:
1. It abolished dyarchy in the provinces and introduced provincial autonomy.
2. It successfully established the All-India Federation exactly as envisaged in the Act.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect — the proposed All-India Federation never came into being since the princely states did not join it.

intermediate.q:
Consider the following statements about the Government of India Act of 1935:
1. It provided for a Federal Court, which was set up in 1937.
2. It provided for the establishment of the Reserve Bank of India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Both statements are correct. The Government of India Act, 1935 provided for both the Federal Court (1937) and the Reserve Bank of India.

intermediate.q:
Consider the following statements about the Indian Independence Act of 1947:
1. It abolished the office of Viceroy and provided for a Governor-General in each new dominion.
2. It deprived the Governor-General of the power to assent to bills in the name of the King.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect — the Act actually took away the British Monarch's veto/reservation power over bills, while the Governor-General retained full power to assent to bills in the King's name.

intermediate.q:
Consider the following statements about the Interim Government (1946) and the First Cabinet of Independent India (1947):
1. Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel held the Home portfolio in both governments.
2. Dr. B.R. Ambedkar was a member of the Interim Government of 1946.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect — Dr. B.R. Ambedkar joined only the First Cabinet of 1947 as Law Minister; the Law portfolio in the 1946 Interim Government was held by Jogendra Nath Mandal.

intermediate.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The East India Company obtained 'diwani' rights over Bengal, Bihar and Orissa after its victory in the Battle of Buxar (1764).
2. The boundary between India and Pakistan in 1947 was determined by a Boundary Commission headed by Cyril Radcliffe.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Both statements are correct. The Mughal Emperor Shah Alam granted 'diwani' after the Battle of Buxar (1764), and the India-Pakistan boundary was fixed by a commission headed by Radcliffe.

advanced.q:
Arrange the following in chronological order of enactment:
1. Pitt's India Act
2. Regulating Act
3. Charter Act of 1833
4. Government of India Act, 1858
advanced.e: Correct chronological order: Regulating Act (1773) → Pitt's India Act (1784) → Charter Act of 1833 → Government of India Act, 1858.

advanced.q: Which of the following is NOT a correct feature of the Regulating Act of 1773?
o: It created a four-member Executive Council to assist the Governor-General of Bengal
It provided for a Supreme Court at Calcutta with a chief justice and three other judges
It abolished the office of Governor-General of Bengal that it had itself created
It subordinated the Bombay and Madras presidencies to the Governor-General of Bengal
advanced.e: The Act created the office of Governor-General of Bengal — it did not abolish it. All the other listed features are genuine provisions of the Regulating Act, 1773.

advanced.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Indian Councils Act of 1861 provided for new legislative councils for Bengal, the North-Western Provinces, and Punjab.
2. The Indian Councils Act of 1909 raised the size of the Central legislative council from 16 to 60 members.
3. The Government of India Act of 1919 replaced the Indian legislative council with a bicameral legislature.
How many of the above statements are correct?
advanced.e: All three statements are correct — new councils under the 1861 Act, expansion to 60 members under the 1909 Act, and the bicameral legislature (Council of State + Legislative Assembly) under the 1919 Act.

advanced.q: The Charter Act of 1833 gave the Governor-General of India exclusive legislative power over all of British India. Which later Act specifically added a separate legislative wing with dedicated 'legislative councillors', distinct from the Governor-General's executive council?
advanced.e: The Charter Act of 1853 added six new 'legislative councillors' and, for the first time, separated the legislative and executive functions of the Governor-General's council into a distinct Indian (Central) Legislative Council.

advanced.q:
Consider the following statements about the Communal Award (1932) and the Poona Pact:
1. Ramsay MacDonald announced the Communal Award in August 1932.
2. The Poona Pact was an agreement between the Indian National Congress and Dr. B.R. Ambedkar.
3. The Poona Pact extended separate electorates to the depressed classes for the first time.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect — it was the Communal Award, not the Poona Pact, that extended separate electorates to the depressed classes; the Poona Pact instead dropped that provision in favour of joint electorates with reserved seats.

advanced.q: The Charter Act of 1833 attempted, but failed, to introduce open competition for civil service recruitment. Which subsequent Act actually implemented open competition, leading to the appointment of the Macaulay Committee in 1854?
advanced.e: The Charter Act of 1853 introduced open competition for the covenanted civil service, following which the Macaulay Committee (Committee on the Indian Civil Service) was appointed in 1854.

advanced.q: Which of the following was NOT a feature of the Government of India Act, 1919?
o: It created the office of the High Commissioner for India in London
It separated provincial budgets from the Central budget for the first time
It provided for a statutory commission to review its working after ten years
It introduced joint electorates for all communities, abolishing separate electorates
advanced.e: The 1919 Act actually extended separate electorates further, to Sikhs, Indian Christians, Anglo-Indians and Europeans — it did not abolish them. All the other options are genuine features of the Act.

advanced.q: Which of the following is correctly identified as a change introduced by the Government of India Act, 1919, that had NOT been introduced by any earlier Act discussed in this chapter?
o: Bicameralism and direct election in the central legislature
The portfolio system for departmental administration
Abolition of dyarchy in the provinces
advanced.e: Bicameralism and direct elections at the Centre were introduced for the first time by the 1919 Act. Separate Muslim electorates (1909) and the portfolio system (1861, recognising Canning's 1859 practice) predate it, while dyarchy was introduced, not abolished, by this Act.

advanced.q: The recommendations of which body, formed to consider the Simon Commission's proposals through three Round Table Conferences and a White Paper on Constitutional Reforms, were substantially incorporated into the Government of India Act, 1935?
o: The Joint Select Committee of the British Parliament
advanced.e: After the Round Table Conferences and the White Paper, a Joint Select Committee of the British Parliament examined the proposals, and its recommendations (with changes) were incorporated into the Government of India Act, 1935.

advanced.q: The British Government's declaration of 20 August 1917, announcing the gradual introduction of 'responsible government' in India, was a precursor to which Act?
advanced.e: The 1917 declaration of gradually developing self-governing institutions led directly to the Government of India Act, 1919 (Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms).

advanced.q: Under the Indian Independence Act, 1947, the British Monarch was deprived of the right to veto bills or reserve them for royal approval. In whom was this power instead vested?
o: The Secretary of State for Commonwealth Affairs
No one — the power was abolished entirely
advanced.e: The Act took away the Monarch's veto/reservation power over bills, giving the Governor-General of each dominion full power to assent to bills in the King's name.

advanced.q:
Consider the following statements about the legislative lists created by the Government of India Act, 1935:
1. The Federal List contained 59 items.
2. The Provincial List contained 54 items.
3. Residuary powers under the Concurrent List were vested in the provinces.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect — residuary powers were vested in the Viceroy (Governor-General), not the provinces.

advanced.q: Which Act first separated provincial budgets from the Central budget, authorising provincial legislatures to enact their own budgets?
advanced.e: The Government of India Act, 1919 separated provincial budgets from the Central budget for the first time, authorising provincial legislatures to pass their own budgets.

advanced.q: Under the dyarchy scheme of the Government of India Act, 1919, which of the following pairs is correctly matched with its mode of administration?
o: Reserved subjects (police, justice, finance) — administered by the Governor with ministers responsible to the legislature
Transferred subjects (health, education, agriculture) — administered by the Governor with ministers responsible to the legislature
Reserved subjects — administered by the Governor and executive council, without responsibility to the legislature
Transferred subjects — administered directly by the Secretary of State for India
advanced.e: Reserved subjects (police, justice, prisons, land revenue, finance) were administered by the Governor and his executive council without being responsible to the legislature, while transferred subjects were run by ministers who were so responsible.

advanced.q: Which Act specifically provided for the establishment of a Federal Public Service Commission, a Provincial Public Service Commission, and a Joint Public Service Commission — distinct from the Central Public Service Commission set up in 1926?
advanced.e: While the 1919 Act led to the Central Public Service Commission being set up in 1926, it was the Government of India Act, 1935 that specifically provided for Federal, Provincial, and Joint Public Service Commissions.

advanced.q:
Consider the following statements about portfolio holders in 1946-47:
1. Liaquat Ali Khan held the Finance portfolio in the Interim Government of 1946.
2. R.K. Shanmugham Chetty held the Finance portfolio in the First Cabinet of 1947.
3. Dr. John Mathai held Industries and Supplies in the Interim Government and Railways and Transport in the First Cabinet.
How many of the above statements are correct?
advanced.e: All three are correct: Liaquat Ali Khan (Finance, Interim Govt.), R.K. Shanmugham Chetty (Finance, First Cabinet), and Dr. John Mathai, who moved from Industries and Supplies to Railways and Transport between the two governments.

advanced.q: Unlike every Charter Act before it, the Charter Act of 1853 did not specify a fixed term for renewal of the East India Company's rule. What was the constitutional significance of this omission?
o: It indicated the Company's rule could be terminated by Parliament at any time it wished
It meant the Company's rule became permanent and irrevocable
It transferred the renewal decision to the Board of Control instead of Parliament
It had no practical significance and was a drafting oversight
advanced.e: By not fixing a renewal period, the Charter Act of 1853 signalled that the Company's rule could be terminated by Parliament at any time it chose, unlike the fixed 20-year terms of earlier Charter Acts.

advanced.q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Indian Councils Act of 1861 from the centralising trend of earlier Acts?
o: It continued the centralisation begun by the Regulating Act of 1773 and completed by the Charter Act of 1833
It reversed that centralising trend by restoring legislative powers to the Bombay and Madras presidencies
It abolished all provincial legislative councils entirely
It transferred all legislative power to the Secretary of State for India
advanced.e: The Indian Councils Act, 1861 reversed the centralising tendency (started by the Regulating Act of 1773, peaking under the Charter Act of 1833) by restoring legislative powers to Bombay and Madras.

upsc.q:
With reference to the Regulating Act of 1773, consider the following statements:
1. It created a four-member Executive Council to assist the Governor-General of Bengal.
2. It subordinated the Governors of Bombay and Madras to the Governor-General of Bengal in matters of war, peace and revenue.
3. It permitted Company servants to accept gifts from Indian rulers, subject to disclosure.
How many of the above statements are correct?
upsc.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect — the Act prohibited Company servants from accepting presents or bribes from 'natives' altogether, with no disclosure exception.

upsc.q:
Assertion (A): The Amending Act of 1781 exempted the Governor-General-in-Council from the Supreme Court's jurisdiction for their official acts.
Reason (R): The Act also excluded revenue matters entirely from the Supreme Court's jurisdiction.
Which one of the following is correct?
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
upsc.e: Both are independently true provisions of the Amending Act, 1781 (Act of Settlement), but R does not explain A — they are two separate, unrelated restrictions placed on the Supreme Court's jurisdiction.

upsc.q:
Match List-I (Act) with List-II (a key feature) and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I:
A. Regulating Act, 1773
B. Pitt's India Act, 1784
C. Charter Act, 1833
D. Government of India Act, 1858
List-II:
1. Ended the East India Company's existence as a commercial body
2. Created the Board of Control for political affairs
3. Established the Supreme Court at Calcutta
4. Abolished the Board of Control and Court of Directors, transferring power to the Crown
upsc.e: Regulating Act (1773) — Supreme Court at Calcutta; Pitt's India Act (1784) — Board of Control; Charter Act (1833) — Company became purely administrative; GoI Act (1858) — abolished Board of Control & Court of Directors, transferring power to the Crown.

upsc.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the progressive curtailment of the East India Company's trade privileges:
1. The Charter Act of 1793 renewed the Company's trade monopoly for a further 20 years.
2. The Charter Act of 1813 ended the Company's monopoly over all trade, including tea and trade with China.
3. The Charter Act of 1833 ended the Company's commercial activities altogether, making it a purely administrative body.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
upsc.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is incorrect — the Charter Act of 1813 ended the general trade monopoly but continued the Company's monopoly over tea trade and trade with China; that exception was removed only later, by the 1833 Act.

upsc.q: With reference to the Charter Act of 1833, which one of the following statements is NOT correct?
o: It made the Governor-General of Bengal the Governor-General of India
It deprived the Governors of Bombay and Madras of their legislative powers
Its attempt to introduce open competition for civil service selection was implemented successfully without opposition
It vested the Government of India, for the first time, with authority over the entire British-held territory in India
upsc.e: The 1833 Act's open-competition provision was negated after opposition from the Court of Directors and not actually implemented at the time — the other three statements are correct features of the Act.

upsc.q:
Consider the following statements about the Charter Act of 1853:
1. It was the first Act to separate the legislative and executive functions of the Governor-General's council.
2. It introduced open competition for the covenanted civil service, leading to the Macaulay Committee of 1854.
3. It renewed the Company's charter for a fixed period of 20 years, similar to the Charter Act of 1793.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
upsc.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect — unlike the 1793 Act, the Charter Act of 1853 fixed no definite period for renewal, signalling Parliament could end Company rule whenever it wished.

upsc.q:
Assertion (A): The Government of India Act, 1858 is regarded as having made no substantial change to India's system of government.
Reason (R): The Act was chiefly concerned with improving the machinery by which the Indian Government was superintended and controlled in England.
Which one of the following is correct?
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
upsc.e: The Government of India Act, 1858 mainly transferred power from Company to Crown and reorganised control machinery in England (Secretary of State, Council of India) without substantially altering how India itself was governed — R correctly explains A.

upsc.q:
Consider the following statements about the Indian Councils Act of 1861:
1. It began associating Indians with law-making through nomination of non-official members.
2. It restored legislative powers to the Bombay and Madras presidencies, reversing an earlier centralising trend.
3. It empowered the Viceroy to issue ordinances during an emergency, valid for six months.
How many of the above statements are correct?
upsc.e: All three are correct features of the Indian Councils Act, 1861: Indian nomination to councils, decentralisation to Bombay/Madras, and the Viceroy's six-month emergency ordinance power.

upsc.q: With reference to the Indian Councils Act of 1892, which one of the following statements is correct?
o: It introduced direct elections to the legislative councils for the first time
It provided a limited, indirect form of election, without using the word 'election' anywhere in the Act
It gave the legislative councils a non-official majority at the Centre
It abolished the official majority in the provincial legislative councils
upsc.e: The Indian Councils Act, 1892 allowed indirect, limited nomination on the recommendation of bodies like district boards and universities — described as nomination, not election — while retaining official majorities.

upsc.q:
Consider the following statements about the Indian Councils Act of 1909 (Morley-Minto Reforms):
1. It raised the size of the Central legislative council from 16 to 60 members.
2. It allowed the provincial legislative councils, but not the Central legislative council, to have a non-official majority.
3. Satyendra Prasad Sinha became the first Indian member of the Viceroy's Executive Council, appointed as the Law Member.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
upsc.e: All three statements are correct features of the Morley-Minto Reforms, 1909 — central council enlarged to 60, non-official majority only provincially, and Sinha as first Indian Law Member on the Viceroy's council.

upsc.q:
Assertion (A): The Government of India Act, 1919 is considered to have relaxed central control over the provinces.
Reason (R): It classified all subjects of administration into central and provincial subjects through the 'Devolution Rules'.
Which one of the following is correct?
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
upsc.e: The Devolution Rules under the 1919 Act delegated authority from the Centre to the provinces by classifying subjects, which directly relaxed central control — R correctly explains A.

upsc.q:
With reference to 'dyarchy' as introduced by the Government of India Act, 1919, consider the following statements:
1. Transferred subjects were administered by the Governor with the aid of ministers responsible to the legislative council.
2. Reserved subjects were administered by the Governor and his executive council without responsibility to the legislative council.
3. Police, justice, and finance were classified as transferred subjects.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
upsc.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect — police, administration of justice, prisons, land revenue and finance were classified as reserved subjects, not transferred.

upsc.q:
Consider the following pairs of 'firsts' introduced by various constitutional Acts:
1. Bicameralism and direct election at the Centre — Government of India Act, 1919
2. Separate electorate for Muslims — Indian Councils Act, 1909
3. Recognition of the portfolio system — Indian Councils Act, 1861
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
upsc.e: All three pairs are correctly matched: bicameralism/direct election (1919), Muslim separate electorate (1909), and legal recognition of the portfolio system, which Canning had introduced administratively in 1859 (1861 Act).

upsc.q: With reference to the Simon Commission (1927) and its aftermath, which one of the following sequences is correct?
o: Simon Commission → Round Table Conferences → White Paper on Constitutional Reforms → Joint Select Committee → Government of India Act, 1935
Round Table Conferences → Simon Commission → Joint Select Committee → White Paper → Government of India Act, 1935
Simon Commission → Joint Select Committee → Round Table Conferences → White Paper → Government of India Act, 1935
White Paper → Simon Commission → Round Table Conferences → Joint Select Committee → Government of India Act, 1935
upsc.e: The correct sequence: the Simon Commission's 1930 report was followed by Round Table Conferences, leading to a White Paper, examined by a Joint Select Committee, whose recommendations shaped the Government of India Act, 1935.

upsc.q:
Consider the following statements about the Communal Award (1932) and the Poona Pact:
1. The Communal Award extended separate electorates to the depressed classes, in addition to Muslims, Sikhs, Indian Christians, Anglo-Indians and Europeans.
2. Gandhi's fast unto death in Yerawada Jail was directed against separate electorates for Muslims.
3. The Poona Pact retained joint Hindu electorates while reserving seats for the depressed classes.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
upsc.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is incorrect — Gandhi's fast specifically opposed the extension of separate electorates to the depressed classes, not to Muslims.

upsc.q:
With reference to the Government of India Act, 1935, consider the following statements:
1. It divided legislative powers between the Centre and units through Federal, Provincial and Concurrent Lists.
2. Residuary powers under the Act were vested in the provincial legislatures.
3. The proposed All-India Federation did not come into being because the required princely states did not accede to it.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
upsc.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is incorrect — residuary powers under the Government of India Act, 1935 were vested in the Viceroy (Governor-General), not the provincial legislatures.

upsc.q:
Match List-I (institution) with List-II (the Act that established or provided for it), and select the correct answer using the codes below:
List-I:
A. Federal Court
B. Reserve Bank of India
C. Central Public Service Commission
D. Federal, Provincial & Joint Public Service Commissions
List-II:
1. Government of India Act, 1919
2. Government of India Act, 1935
3. Government of India Act, 1935
4. Government of India Act, 1935
upsc.e: The Federal Court and RBI were both provided for by the 1935 Act; the Central PSC traces to the 1919 Act (set up in 1926); the Federal/Provincial/Joint PSCs were a distinct 1935 Act provision.

upsc.q:
Assertion (A): The Indian Independence Act, 1947 abolished the office of Viceroy.
Reason (R): It empowered the British Monarch to directly govern the two new dominions of India and Pakistan until their own constitutions were framed.
Which one of the following is correct?
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
upsc.e: A is correct — the office of Viceroy was abolished, replaced by a Governor-General for each dominion. R is false — the Act explicitly stated His Majesty's Government in Britain would have no responsibility for governing India or Pakistan.

upsc.q:
Consider the following statements about the transition of power in August 1947:
1. The Constituent Assembly of India, formed in 1946, became the Parliament of the Indian Dominion after independence.
2. Lord Mountbatten became the first Governor-General of the Dominion of India.
3. The Indian Independence Act, 1947 fixed the composition of the Constituent Assembly at exactly 389 members even after Partition.
How many of the above statements are correct?
upsc.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect and is, in any case, outside the scope of this chapter — the Constituent Assembly's composition and its post-Partition changes belong to 'Making of the Constitution', not this Act's provisions on transfer of power.

upsc.q:
With reference to portfolios held across the Interim Government (1946) and the First Cabinet of Independent India (1947), consider the following statements:
1. Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel held the Home portfolio in both governments, gaining the States portfolio only in 1947.
2. Dr. John Mathai moved from Industries and Supplies in 1946 to Railways and Transport in 1947.
3. Jagjivan Ram held the Labour portfolio in both the Interim Government and the First Cabinet.
How many of the above statements are correct?
upsc.e: All three are correct: Patel added the States portfolio in 1947; Dr. John Mathai moved from Industries & Supplies to Railways & Transport; Jagjivan Ram retained Labour in both governments.
